newsitem.title: UK: Peter Wood leaves Direct Line.
newsitem.headline: Peter Wood leaves Direct Line.

text.p: Peter Wood, the multi-millionaire founder of Direct Line, which pioneered telephone selling of insurance in Britain, on Wednesday left the company, its parent Royal Bank of Scotland said.
Wood, who started the venture 11 years ago with just 20 million pounds ($33 million) of capital from Royal Bank, will be succeeded by his deputy Ian Chippendale.

Royal Bank said Wood was leaving to develop his growing business interests in the U.S., Britain and Spain. He has been developing a new auto insurer in the U.S. called Direct Response and also plans a home insurance venture called Home Owners Corp.

After recording spectacular profits, which brought Wood huge and controversial salary payments, Direct Line has recently suffered from the cut-throat competition in the insurance market which has restricted its profitability.

Royal Bank said Wood, who has a large shareholding in Royal Bank, had been scaling down his involvement with Direct Line. He will receive no payment for the remainder of his contract but an unspecified payment is to be made to his pension fund "in recognition of his contribution to Direct Line."

Chippendale was made deputy chief executive of Direct Line in January and has been chief executive of Direct Line Insurance since March 1996. He was previously with Privilege Insurance and Provident Financial. ($ = 0.599 British Pounds)
